Subject: Elevated error rate + logs request for May 17 incident

Marissa —

Following up from our incident yesterday evening: between ~2026-05-17T22:14:00Z and 2026-05-17T22:48:00Z we saw sustained 5xx errors and a sharp drop in throughput on the FinOps production integration (integration id: FIN-INT-77). Our security and compliance teams require the following evidence for an internal post-mortem and an external regulator inquiry:

- Request/response time series (1-minute granularity) for the window above
- Sampled request logs (redacted if needed) showing status codes, request IDs, and latency
- Audit trail of which Redwood employees accessed raw logs during the incident
- Confirmation of retention policy for request bodies and whether any customer data in request payloads is retained or logged in plaintext

Can you indicate what you can provide by EOD tomorrow? If you need an NDA or access form to be signed before sharing redacted logs, please advise.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Head of Security — FinOps, Inc.

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>

Cc: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@finops.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Elevated error rate + logs request for May 17 incident

Marissa / all —

Quick technical summary (short):
- Root cause: transient routing thrash that caused excessive backfills to the KV cache on our serving tier leading to CPU throttling for a subset of worker pods (manifested as increased tail latency and 5xx on a small percentage of requests).
- Affected window: 2026-05-17T22:14:00Z -> 2026-05-17T22:48:00Z (matches customer report).
- Impact: throughput reduced ~27% for the customers traffic; error rate peaked at ~6.1% for 503/504s for that integration id.

Logs and retention:
- What we persist by default (hosted): request metadata (timestamps, request_id, model_variant, token_count, response_code), traces (sampling), and encrypted request/response bodies retained for 30 days unless the customer has configured log-redaction or opted-out. Bodies are encrypted at rest and access is auditable.
- We do NOT store long-term plaintext customer data in an unencrypted index; raw bodies are in an encrypted blobstore and are only accessible to authorized engineers via an approval workflow.

What I can produce immediately:
- A redacted access_log_excerpt.csv (sample) covering the window with request_id, timestamp, latency_ms, response_code, worker_id (redacted), and a hashed request fingerprint (no plaintext prompt). Ive attached a short incident timeline PDF that summarizes observed behavior.
- A list of internal accounts that accessed the storage bucket for the blobstore during the window (requires Evelyn to pull audit logs) — I can pre-filter and provide that as an export.

Attachments referenced: access_log_excerpt.csv (sample), redwood_incident_timeline.pdf

Let me know if FinOps needs additional artifact formats (Parquet/CSV) and Ill export.

- David
David Kim
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>

Marissa / Elena —

I pulled the compliance artifacts. Summary:
- SOC2: we can share the relevant control excerpts that describe log retention, encryption, and access controls. Ive attached soc2_audit_excerpt.pdf (redacted).
- Audit trail: we have IAM and KMS access logs for the blobstore covering 2026-05-17T21:00:00Z -> 2026-05-18T00:30:00Z showing which internal identities requested/decrypted blobs. I will export a CSV of the principal, action, timestamp, and justification (if present) and include it in the package.
- Data handling: request/response bodies are retained 30 days by default. For customers that require stricter retention/redaction we honor contractual settings; FinOps currently is on default retention per our records.

Sharing plan and constraints:
1) We will provide redacted logs (no plaintext prompts) and access audit CSV as a secure share.
2) Because this contains potentially sensitive customer payloads, our legal team prefers a short Data Access Agreement (standard DocuSign) that FinOps signs before we share the full audit package. If FinOps prefers only the high-level artifacts (timeline, redacted CSV, SOC2 excerpt), we can provide those immediately without an additional DocuSign.
3) All artifacts will be shared via the secure Drive folder and access will be time-limited to the FinOps domain.

Ill prepare the audit CSV and place the artifacts in a restricted Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-finops-incident (view-only; access granted after confirmation).

Evelyn Hart
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
